fix: Adopt the windowed set whenever it is non-empty and still clears the downstream min-strike guard, e.g. `if len(windowed) >= _MIN_STRIKES: clean = windowed` else fall back only if `len(windowed) < _MIN_STRIKES and len(windowed) > 0` is acceptable — preferably trim to the contiguous run around spot rather than reverting to the full chain. At minimum, prefer `clean = windowed if windowed else clean`.

title: MVN path: np.cov 1-D branch reshapes a multi-asset variance vector to a 1x1 matrix
description: In _simulate_paths_mvn, cov = np.cov(R, rowvar=False). For a single asset cov.ndim==0 (scalar) and is handled. But the `elif cov.ndim == 1: cov = cov.reshape(1,1)` branch is wrong: np.cov never returns a 1-D array for a 2-D input with >1 column (it returns an (N,N) matrix), and if it ever did (e.g. an accidental 1-row R giving a length-N variance vector) reshape(1,1) would crash for N>1 or silently drop assets. The branch can corrupt the covariance for the multi-asset case it appears intended to guard.
fix: Drop the ndim==1 branch (it cannot legitimately occur for a (T,N) matrix), or replace it with `cov = np.atleast_2d(cov)` so an N-length vector becomes (1,N) and fails loudly rather than being silently squashed to (1,1). Keep only the ndim==0 single-asset guard.

title: Form 4 index fallback fetches `-index.json` which the module's own docs say does not exist
description: In get_form4_transactions._parse_one_form4, when primary_doc is empty it builds `index_url = .../{acc_nodash}-index.json` and parses `idx_data.get('documents', [])`. But _best_document_from_index (same file, line 374-385) explicitly documents 'the -index.json URL does not exist on EDGAR' and parses the -index.html instead. So this JSON fallback path always 404s (caught by the bare except → pass), leaving primary_doc empty, and the function returns [] — silently dropping every Form 4 whose submissions JSON had no primaryDocument. Insider data for those filings is lost.
fix: Mirror _best_document_from_index: build the dashed accession and fetch `{acc_dashed}-index.html`, parse the table for a row whose type is '4' and filename ends in .xml, and use that as primary_doc. Or call _best_document_from_index(cik_int, acc_nodash, '4') and use its return. Do not rely on the nonexistent -index.json.

title: _score_insiders/_score_ml_forecast tuple unpack assumes parallel_map slot is a 2-tuple, but a partial failure can return a non-tuple
description: In _compute_score_uncached, `insider_score, insider_txns = part[0] if part[0] is not None else (12, [])` and `ml_score, ml_detail = part[3] if part[3] is not None else (10, {...})`. parallel_map returns None for a slot whose work fn RAISED (handled). But _score_insiders and _score_ml_forecast themselves return a 2-tuple on success and on their own internal except. The hazard: if either function returns a single value on some path (e.g. a future refactor) or if safe_executor returns a partial/exception sentinel that is truthy-but-not-a-2-tuple, the tuple unpack raises ValueError/TypeError, aborting the whole score with a 500 despite the per-component try/except design intent. Currently both functions are disciplined, so confidence on an active crash is medium; it is a latent fragility where the None-guard does not also guard against wrong-arity returns.
fix: Guard the arity, not just None: `res = part[0]; insider_score, insider_txns = res if isinstance(res, tuple) and len(res) == 2 else (12, [])` and likewise for part[3], so a malformed slot degrades to the neutral default instead of raising.

title: Optimizer verdict compares candidate's whole-book fraction against optimizer weight from a partial universe
description: _optimizer_verdict runs markowitz over only `symbols = {current symbols} ∪ {candidate}` and takes `optimal = weights[cand_sym]` as the target weight, then compares it to `proposed_size = cand_mv / proposed_nav`. But proposed_nav is the full proposed book NAV (sum of every holding's market_value), while the optimizer's weights are a re-optimized allocation over that same symbol set that ignores the user's actual current sizes and any cash. The optimizer's 'optimal weight' and the user's 'actual fraction of book' are computed on incompatible bases, so the OVERSIZED/UNDERSIZED/AVOID verdict can be systematically wrong (e.g. a name the optimizer wants at 40% but that's only 5% of a cash-heavy book is flagged UNDERSIZED even when the user intends a small tactical position).
fix: Make the two quantities comparable: compare the optimizer's optimal weight against the candidate's fraction of the optimizer's invested universe (sum of market_values of just `symbols`), not the whole proposed_nav — i.e. `proposed_size = cand_mv / sum(h['market_value'] for h in proposed if h['symbol'] in symbols)`. Or document explicitly that the verdict is 'fraction-of-full-book vs fully-invested-optimal' and is only meaningful for a near-fully-invested book.

title: Congress sell filter `txn_type_raw.startswith('S')` also catches 'SE' (Sale Exercise) but MISSES nothing while purchase filter MISSES 'PE'-prefixed exchange edge
description: In _score_congress_cluster, purchases = txn_type_raw in ('P','PE') and sales = txn_type_raw.startswith('S'). startswith('S') correctly captures 'S','S (partial)','S (Exchange)','SE'. However it ALSO would capture any future 'S'-prefixed code, and critically it does not capture 'E (Exchange)' as a sale even though congress.get_congress_summary classifies 'E (Exchange)' under sells. More concretely, the `n_purchases == 0 and sales` branch sets score=5 (bearish) — but `sales` here is a list truthiness; an 'E (Exchange)' trade (neither purchase nor startswith-S) leaves both purchases and sales empty, so a ticker with only exchange activity falls through to score=10 instead of reflecting the exchange. Minor divergence from the summary module's taxonomy.
fix: Align with congress.get_congress_summary's classification: treat raw in ('P','PE') as buys and raw in ('S','S (partial)','SE','S (Exchange)','E (Exchange)') as sells, instead of startswith('S'), so exchange variants are handled consistently across modules.

title: tts_speech LRU eviction can evict the entry just inserted under concurrent inserts because the while-pop runs under lock but iterates oldest-first including the new key
description: After `_tts_cache[ck] = audio`, the eviction loop `while len(_tts_cache) > _TTS_CACHE_MAX: _tts_cache.pop(next(iter(_tts_cache)))` pops the OLDEST insertion-order key. That's correct in isolation. But the LRU-refresh path on a cache HIT (lines 408-409) pops-then-reinserts ck to move it to the end; if two threads race a hit and a miss for different keys, insertion order can momentarily place a freshly-synthesized (paid) entry near the front, and a concurrent miss's eviction pops it immediately — wasting the just-paid synthesis. The hit-refresh and miss-insert are under separate lock acquisitions, so ordering is not atomic across the read-modify-write.
fix: Perform the hit-refresh (pop+reinsert) and the miss insert+evict within a single _tts_lock critical section that also re-checks membership, so an entry written under the lock is never evicted by a racing operation that observed stale ordering.

title: _parse_date slices the date string to 11 chars, truncating long month-name dates
description: _parse_date does `datetime.strptime(s[:11].strip(), fmt)` for the formats including `"%b %d, %Y"`. A date like 'September 5, 2026' is 17 chars; `s[:11]` = 'September 5' loses the year and also won't match '%b' (abbreviated month) for long month names, so legitimate earnings dates fail to parse and the earnings-blackout gate (10) silently does not fire for those names. The 11-char slice was presumably sized for 'YYYY-MM-DD' but is applied to all formats.
fix: Don't pre-slice for the non-ISO formats; parse the full string per format (or slice only for the fixed-width ISO branch). E.g. try `datetime.strptime(s.strip(), fmt)` for each fmt, falling back, rather than `s[:11]`.

title: _vol_target_factor unit heuristic inflates genuinely low-vol names
description: _vol_target_factor normalizes annualized vol with `av_pct = av * 100.0 if av < 5.0 else av`, intending to detect a fraction (0.25) vs a percent (25.0). But a real low-volatility instrument whose annualized vol is, say, 4% will be supplied as the percent value 4.0, which is < 5.0 and gets multiplied by 100 to 400%, collapsing the vol-target factor to its 0.25 floor and badly under-sizing the position. The 5.0 boundary conflates 'a fraction' with 'a small percent', so the disambiguation is wrong for genuinely quiet names.
fix: Disambiguate on the source's known convention rather than magnitude. Since portfolio_insights.annualized_vol returns a percent, treat `av` as percent unconditionally (drop the *100 branch), or make the wrappers return a documented unit so the consumer never has to guess.

title: TP-ladder rung-2 marks rung-1 as fired without ever selling its third
description: In extra_exit_signals the TP ladder fires the highest-eligible rung and back-marks all lower rungs as fired (`fired.update({1,2})` at line 566, `{1,2,3}` at line 560). If a position gaps straight to >=1.5x TP without a prior cycle at >=1.0x TP, rung-2 sells half the position and stamps rung-1 fired, so the rung-1 third is never scaled out — and conversely rung-3 (line 560) sells the FULL remaining qty and marks 1&2 fired, which is the intended 'dump the rest', but rung-2's half-sell followed by marking rung-1 fired permanently forecloses the rung-1 scale-out on that position. Net effect: the realized scale-out fractions can deviate from the documented thirds-at-tp/1.5tp/2tp ladder depending on which cycle first observes the gain.
fix: Only mark rungs as fired that were actually executed (e.g. for rung-2 do `fired.add(2)` not `fired.update({1,2})`), and let a later cycle still fire rung-1 if price retraces into its band; or document and intend the back-marking explicitly. Minimal correct change: replace the `fired.update({1,2})` / `{1,2,3}` back-marking with adding only the rung that fired.

title: news analyst can emit an all-null headlines list as evidence
description: `[h.get('title') for h in headlines if isinstance(h, dict)]` keeps entries even when `title` is missing, producing a list like `[null, null, ...]`. After _fmt this becomes the JSON string `[null,null]`, which _run treats as truthy non-empty evidence (passes the `if v` filter), so the model is fed meaningless null headlines and the report is no longer flagged as 'no evidence'. The fundamentals/sentiment paths guard their dict keys; this one does not filter falsy titles.
fix: Filter out missing titles: `[h.get('title') for h in headlines if isinstance(h, dict) and h.get('title')]` (matches the pattern already used in aj_personas.fingpt_sentiment line 107).

title: sentiment FinGPT path bypasses the band_is_sentiment scoring intent without using the numeric prior
description: When fingpt_sentiment is enabled, its dict is dumped verbatim into ev['fingpt'] as raw JSON text and handed to the LLM, but the numeric 0-10 score it computes is never used as a deterministic prior/anchor. The function comment frames it as a 'numeric prior', yet it only becomes free-text the model may ignore. This isn't a crash but defeats the stated purpose of the optional prior; the score is effectively decorative.
fix: If a numeric prior is intended, blend it into the report (e.g. nudge AnalystReport.score toward the fingpt score after _run), or relabel the evidence/comments to 'additional sentiment context' so maintainers don't assume the prior influences scoring. Minimal: keep current behavior but drop the 'numeric prior' wording, or pass the score through to _run for anchoring.

title: forecast_horizon_days of 0 silently falls back to 20 due to `or 20`
description: `int((cfg or {}).get('forecast_horizon_days', 20) or 20)`. If an operator explicitly configures a horizon of 0 (or any falsy-but-intentional value), the `or 20` overrides it to 20. While a 0-day horizon is arguably invalid, the double-default masks misconfiguration silently rather than validating it. Negative values pass straight through to ensemble_forecast unguarded (could cause an engine-side error, swallowed by _safe).
fix: Validate explicitly: read the value, then `horizon = h if isinstance(h, int) and h > 0 else 20`, so 0/negative are normalized intentionally and an unexpected type doesn't silently coerce.

title: _run treats whitespace-only evidence values as present, and empty-evidence path never calls model (intended) but skips low-confidence neutral nuance
description: `ev = {k: v for k, v in evidence.items() if v}` keeps any non-empty string, including whitespace-only or the JSON string '""'/'[]'/'{}' that _fmt can emit for empty engine results (e.g. json.dumps([]) == '[]', which is truthy). So an analyst whose engines all returned empty containers passes the `if not ev` guard, sends '[]'-style empty evidence to the model, and produces a confident-looking report from nothing instead of the intended neutral/low-confidence fallback.
fix: Filter out trivially-empty serialized evidence: treat values in {'', '[]', '{}', '""', 'null'} as absent, e.g. `ev = {k: v for k, v in evidence.items() if v and v not in ('[]','{}','""','null')}`.

title: build_briefing sorts radar scores without the NaN guard rank_universe uses
description: build_briefing ranks the universe with `sorted(((s, aj_alpha._radar_score(s)) ...), key=lambda t: -t[1])`. aj_alpha.rank_universe() deliberately added a `_score_key` that coerces non-floats and sinks NaN to the bottom for stable ordering, but build_briefing duplicates the ranking with a raw `-t[1]` key. If `_radar_score` ever yields a NaN (e.g. from a degenerate price series feeding momentum_score / pct_return), NaN comparisons are non-total and the resulting top-K ordering is undefined, so the pre-market briefing can surface the wrong ideas. The two code paths that should rank identically don't.
fix: Reuse the same NaN-safe key as rank_universe: sort with a key that does `fv = float(score); return float('inf') if (math.isnan(fv)) else -fv`, or simply call/extract aj_alpha's `_score_key` helper instead of `lambda t: -t[1]`.

title: _nth_weekday clamps to the last occurrence when the Nth weekday does not exist, yielding a wrong holiday date
description: _nth_weekday returns `days[min(n-1, len(days)-1)]` (line 396). If a month has fewer than n occurrences of the weekday (cannot happen for the holidays currently requested, but the helper is generic), it silently returns the LAST occurrence rather than None, producing an incorrect holiday date. Combined with _us_market_holidays only filtering by year (line 437), a miscomputed date could mark a wrong trading day as a holiday. The fail-safe is 'closed', so impact is limited to occasionally treating a real trading day as closed, but the clamp masks the error rather than degrading cleanly.
fix: Return None when the requested occurrence does not exist: `return days[n-1] if len(days) >= n else None` (the caller already drops None entries), so a missing Nth weekday is omitted rather than aliased to the last one.

title: Evidence/memory text containing literal braces can break str.format in debate prompts
description: The bull/bear prompt is built with `.format(ev=reports_md, mem=mem, opp=...)`. `reports_md` is rendered analyst output and `mem` is recalled memory text — both can contain `{` or `}` characters (e.g. JSON snippets, code, math). Although the substituted VALUES are safe (they are arguments, not the template), the template literal itself is fine; however note the sys prompt uses `.format(symbol=symbol)` on _BULL_SYS/_BEAR_SYS which contain no other braces, so that is safe. The genuine risk is only if reports_md were ever used as a format string elsewhere. Lower severity but worth noting the pattern of mixing untrusted text near format templates.
fix: No change needed if values are only passed as format args (current code is safe). To harden, prefer f-strings or string concatenation for prompt assembly so untrusted content is never adjacent to a format template; document the invariant.

title: research_debate round index counts bull and bear of the same exchange as the same round, but bear is logged before bull's response is seen
description: round is `i // 2`, so turn 0 (bull) and turn 1 (bear) are both round 0 — intended. However the bear at turn 1 rebuts the bull of the SAME round, while the bull at turn 2 (round 1) rebuts the bear of round 0. The pairing is consistent, so this is correct; the only subtle issue is that with rounds=1 there is exactly one bull + one bear (2 turns) which is the intended hard cap. No off-by-one in the loop bound `range(2*rounds)`. Flagging only that the 'round' field semantics (bull and bear share a round number) may surprise downstream consumers expecting one turn per round.
fix: If downstream code (persistence/UI) assumes unique round per turn, document that bull/bear share a round index, or number turns sequentially. No logic change required.

title: compare_by_role ok_rate denominator differs from model_leaderboard (NULL-ok rows deflate it)
description: model_leaderboard() was deliberately fixed to divide oks by `ok_rows` (rows where ok IS NOT NULL) so NULL-ok telemetry can't deflate the rate, but compare_by_role() divides `SUM(ok)` by `calls` (all rows). If any aj_routing rows have a NULL `ok` (legacy rows, or any future writer that doesn't set it — route() always writes 0/1, but external/legacy inserts may not), the per-role ok_rate is understated relative to the leaderboard, and recommend_demotions / A-B adoption decisions read inconsistent numbers for the same model.
fix: Mirror the leaderboard: add `SUM(CASE WHEN ok IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) AS ok_rows` to the compare_by_role query and compute `ok_rate = (oks or 0) / ok_rows if ok_rows else None` so both surfaces use the same NULL-safe denominator.

title: cancel_all_open counts a paper cancel even when the CAS state transition lost the race
description: For paper orders the code does `_set_state(oid, 'canceled'); n += 1` unconditionally (lines 456-457). _set_state returns False when a concurrent writer already moved the order to a terminal state (compare-and-set lost), yet n is still incremented. The returned 'orders_canceled' count (surfaced by kill_switch in its critical alert) can therefore overstate how many orders were actually canceled, masking orders that another thread terminated differently.
fix: Guard the increment on the transition result: `if _set_state(oid, 'canceled'): n += 1` (mirror the live branch which already only counts on a confirmed terminal cancel).

title: Fill audit records raw, uncoerced fill values that can differ from what was persisted
description: _record_fill inserts coerced numeric values qv/pv/fv into aj_fills (line 259) but the audit() call at line 262 logs the RAW fill.get('qty')/('price')/('fees_usd'), which may be None or a string when the coerced stored value was 0.0. The hash-chained audit (the tamper-evident record of what executed) can therefore disagree with the queryable aj_fills row, undermining the audit-vs-table reconciliation the chain is meant to support.
fix: Audit the same coerced values that were persisted: pass qv/pv/fv (and the resolved `at`) into the audit payload instead of the raw fill.get(...) values.

title: recall() ordering claim vs. implementation: cross-symbol lessons appended after same-symbol, not merged reverse-chronological
description: The docstring promises 'reverse-chronological' results, but the implementation concatenates `reversed(same) + reversed(cross)` — two separately reverse-sorted blocks. The combined list is not globally reverse-chronological: an old same-symbol entry can appear before a newer cross-symbol lesson. Consumers that assume the first item is the single most-recent memory get a same-symbol-biased ordering, which is a defensible product choice but contradicts the documented contract and can mislead the debate-prompt 'most recent lesson' emphasis.
fix: Either fix the docstring to state 'same-symbol recents first, then cross-symbol lessons', or merge-and-sort: `picked = sorted(same + cross, key=lambda e: e['ts'], reverse=True)` before rendering, to honor the stated reverse-chronological contract.

title: notify_fill escapes quotes but not newlines in the osascript string
description: notify_fill builds an AppleScript `display notification "..."` string and escapes backslash and double-quote, but not control characters such as a newline or carriage return embedded in `symbol`/`side`. AppleScript string literals cannot span a raw newline, so a symbol containing a newline (or other AppleScript-meaningful control char) breaks the literal and can alter/abort the osascript command. Symbols are normally validated upstream, but this is the only place untrusted-ish text reaches a shell-interpreted argument; the escaping is incomplete for its stated 'cannot break out of the string literal' intent.
fix: Also strip or escape newlines/CR (and other control chars) before formatting, e.g. `msg = msg.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"','\\"').replace("\n"," ").replace("\r"," ")`, or build the message from a sanitized whitelist of characters.

title: council_topk of 0 silently disables the council with a misleading 'topk reached' brief
description: council_budget['max'] = int(cfg.get('council_topk', 3) or 0) (line 398). If an operator sets council_topk to 0 (or it coerces to 0), _council_advise's check `budget.get('n',0) >= budget.get('max',0)` is `0 >= 0` -> True on the very first BUY, returning proceed with brief 'council topk reached' (aj_operator line 179). The council never runs at all, but the audit/brief says the budget was reached rather than that it was disabled — a misleading operational signal that hides a config that turns the whole advisory layer off.
fix: Distinguish disabled-vs-exhausted: when max<=0 short-circuit with an explicit brief (e.g. 'council topk=0 (disabled)') instead of 'topk reached', or treat council_topk<=0 as council inactive up front so the state is unambiguous in the audit trail.

title: Importing private helpers (_safe, _fmt, _neutral) from aj_analysts creates fragile cross-module coupling
description: aj_personas imports the underscore-prefixed privates `_safe`, `_fmt`, `_neutral` from aj_analysts. Any refactor of those privates (rename/signature change) silently breaks personas, and tooling treats them as non-public. Not a runtime bug today, but a real maintainability defect a reviewer would flag given the council layer is brand new and these helpers are likely to evolve.
fix: Promote the shared helpers into a small public module (e.g. aj_analyst_util) or re-export them under public names, and have both aj_analysts and aj_personas import the public symbols.

title: reconcile divergence compares signed qty but the paper book and broker.positions may disagree on sign convention for shorts
description: reconcile builds local and truth maps with float(p['qty']) / float(p.get('qty') or 0) (line 309-310) and flags any |lq-tq|>1e-6 as a divergence. _local_positions returns the FIFO paper book where short positions carry NEGATIVE qty (aj_positions.paper_book), while a live broker.positions() may report shorts as positive qty with a side field, or omit sign entirely. A sign-convention mismatch would generate a spurious divergence and, for a live venue, trigger aj_risk.halt() (line 323) on every reconcile even when positions actually match.
fix: Normalize sign conventions before comparing: when consuming broker.positions() apply the broker's side/short flag to make qty signed the same way as the paper book (negative for short), or compare absolute exposure plus an explicit side check, so identical positions don't read as a divergence and falsely halt live trading.

title: private-path retry turns a valid max_tokens of 0 into an unbounded completion
description: `retry_tokens = (max_tokens + 256) if max_tokens else None` (also at line 140 in the public path) uses a truthiness test. A caller-supplied `max_tokens=0` is falsy, so the escalation retry passes `max_tokens=None` (unbounded) instead of a bounded budget. That silently removes the token cap on the retry for the one explicit value (0) a caller might use to mean 'no/zero budget', diverging from the first attempt's behavior and inflating cost/latency.
fix: Use an explicit None check: `retry_tokens = (max_tokens + 256) if max_tokens is not None else None` on both line 121 and line 140.

title: time-of-day exit window assumes a 390-min session, wrong on early-close days
description: The ⑫ trade-skip-close gate uses `if mins > (390 - skip_close)` with a hard-coded 390-minute regular session and `_minutes_into_regular()` measured from 09:30 ET. On NYSE early-close days (1:00 PM ET, ~210 minutes) market_session() still returns 'regular', so the 'last N minutes of session' guard is computed against the wrong session length and effectively never engages near the real close. New buys can be placed right at the early close the operator intended to avoid.
fix: Derive the session end dynamically (e.g. compute today's actual regular close, 13:00 ET on half-days vs 16:00 otherwise) and use `(session_len_min - skip_close)` instead of the literal 390, or skip the close-window check when the day is a known early-close date.

title: Code-fence stripping removes the literal substring '```json' anywhere, corrupting JSON string values that contain it
description: `s = re.sub(r'```(?:json)?', '', s)` removes every occurrence of triple-backtick (optionally followed by 'json') from the whole text, including inside JSON string values (e.g. a narrative field describing a code block). This can mangle otherwise-valid JSON whose string content legitimately contains backticks, causing json.loads to fail and the schema to fall back to defaults.
fix: Only strip leading/trailing fences (anchor the regex to start/end after stripping whitespace, e.g. remove a leading '```json'/'```' line and a trailing '```' line) rather than globally substituting every backtick run in the document.

title: from_llm with band_is_sentiment=False stores the raw 'rating' string as a SentimentBand-typed band field, polluting the band column
description: `band = parse_band(band_raw).value if band_is_sentiment else str(band_raw)` where `band_raw = d.get('band') or d.get('sentiment') or d.get('rating') or ''`. For non-sentiment analysts (fundamentals/technical) band_is_sentiment is False, so band becomes the raw string — which may be a Rating value like 'BUY' or arbitrary model text. This free-form value is later persisted to the `aj_analyst_reports.band` column and rendered as a sentiment band, mixing rating vocabulary into the band field and breaking any band-based filtering/aggregation that expects SentimentBand values.
fix: For non-sentiment analysts, either leave band empty or normalize through parse_band as well (treating it as a coarse sentiment), and stop pulling 'rating' into band_raw for sentiment analysts. Keep rating and band in distinct, well-typed fields.

title: Redundant `rev_growth is not None` re-check after early return makes margin-expansion bonus appear conditional when it is not
description: In _score_revenue_momentum, after `if rev_growth is None: return ...` (line 99-100), rev_growth is guaranteed non-None. Yet line 115 re-tests `if earn_growth is not None and rev_growth is not None and earn_growth > rev_growth`. The `rev_growth is not None` clause is always True here — harmless but it signals the author may have intended different gating. Not a runtime bug, but the dead clause obscures intent and risks a future edit assuming rev_growth can be None at this point.
fix: Drop the redundant `and rev_growth is not None` from the line-115 condition since rev_growth cannot be None after the line-99 guard, leaving `if earn_growth is not None and earn_growth > rev_growth:`.

category: race / cache eviction under lock-free read
title: _cget does not evict expired entries, so the negative-cache map grows and stale tuples linger
description: _cget returns None on expiry but never pops the expired key; only _cset evicts (and only when len>100, removing up to 30 already-expired entries). For symbols/subreddits queried once and never again, their expired entries persist until the size threshold triggers a sweep. Combined with _NEG sentinels this is a slow unbounded-ish growth and means an expired _NEG can sit indefinitely; not a correctness bug for callers (they re-fetch on expiry) but a minor memory issue and makes the negative cache's TTL semantics fuzzy.
fix: In _cget, when an entry is found but expired, pop it: `if v is not None and v[1] > time.time(): return v[0]` else `self._cache.pop(k, None); return None` (under the lock), keeping the map bounded by liveness rather than only by the size-triggered sweep.

title: research_track_calls: negative ?limit reaches SQL LIMIT unclamped
description: limit = _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 20) is forwarded to research_tracker.get_recent_calls(signal_name, limit=limit), which binds it to 'LIMIT ?' (research_tracker.py:443). A negative limit again degrades to LIMIT -1 (all rows). Inconsistent with the clamping applied to every other limit-bearing route in this file.
fix: limit = max(1, _safe_int(request.args.get('limit'), 20))

title: _jarvis_act_refund can remove another request's slot (identical timestamps)
description: _jarvis_act_charge sets stamps = [now]*n — all appended timestamps are the SAME float. _jarvis_act_refund then does _JARVIS_ACT_TIMES.remove(t), which removes the first list element EQUAL to t. When two concurrent charges land on the same time.time() value (common at sub-ms resolution under the GIL), a refund by one request can delete the other request's still-valid slot, violating the documented invariant that 'concurrent requests can't refund each other's slots'. Effect: the rolling rate-limit window can be under- or over-counted, occasionally letting an extra confirmed mutating action through (or wrongly rejecting one).
fix: Make each charged stamp unique so remove() targets the caller's own entry — e.g. return monotonically distinct tokens (now + i*1e-9 for i in range(n), or use itertools.count()) and prune the window by an absolute-time field rather than identity.

title: aj_council route can attach the wrong run's reports under concurrency
description: After aj_council.run(symbol, force=True) the route re-queries 'SELECT id FROM aj_council_runs WHERE symbol=? ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1' to find the run it just created, then loads aj_analyst_reports/aj_debate_turns for that id. If the operator cycle (or a second inspection request) creates another council run for the same symbol between run() and this SELECT, the route returns a DIFFERENT run's reports/debate alongside dec.to_audit(), silently mismatching the decision and its supporting transcript.
fix: Have aj_council.run() return the run id it wrote (or surface it on the decision object) and query reports/turns by that exact id instead of re-deriving 'latest for symbol'.

title: jarvis_act batch: charged rate-limit slots not refunded when the batch executor raises
description: The batch path calls _jarvis_act_charge(len(actions)) and then batch_fn(actions); if batch_fn raises, control falls to _err(e) WITHOUT refunding the charged slots. The sibling aj_run_route deliberately refunds on a failed run (lines 3639-3643) precisely so transient failures don't drain the shared budget. Here a single exception (e.g. registry import hiccup) permanently consumes len(actions) of the 10/min budget even though nothing executed.
fix: Wrap: stamps = _jarvis_act_charge(len(actions)); if not stamps: 429; try: r = batch_fn(actions) except Exception as e: _jarvis_act_refund(stamps); return _err(e). (Single-action path at 3935-3940 has the same gap and the same fix.)

title: dividend income_weight is wrong when annual incomes can offset to a near-zero total
description: income_weight = r['annual_income'] / total_annual_income * 100 guards only the exact-zero case (if total_annual_income else 0). div_rate from yfinance is normally >=0 so this is usually fine, but if any feed returns a negative/odd div_rate the per-position weights divide by a total that can be a tiny residual, producing absurd weights (e.g. 5000%). Even without negatives, when total_annual_income is a tiny float dust value the weights blow up. The 'positions with div_rate' headline is unaffected, but the per-row income_weight surfaced to the UI is.
fix: Compute the weight base from a clamped denominator, e.g. base = total_annual_income if total_annual_income > 0 else 0, and skip/zero weights when base <= 0; or clamp div_rate to >= 0 when accumulating annual_income.

title: Daily portfolio snapshot is keyed by UTC date, not market/local date
description: today = _utc_now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d') and db.save_snapshot(date=today, ...) (INSERT OR REPLACE per the comment) buckets the once-per-day snapshot by UTC calendar day. For a US user the UTC day rolls over at 19:00-20:00 ET, so a snapshot taken during the active US trading afternoon is filed under the NEXT calendar day, and an end-of-session valuation can overwrite the 'next day' row before that day actually starts — distorting the history/benchmark series shown in /api/portfolio/history and /api/portfolio/benchmark.
fix: Key the snapshot by the intended local/market date (e.g. America/New_York) instead of UTC: today = datetime.now(ZoneInfo('America/New_York')).strftime('%Y-%m-%d'), keeping the rest of save_snapshot unchanged.

title: Snapshot alert check can miss prices for lowercased alert symbols
description: alert_syms = list({a['symbol'] for a in active_alerts}) uses the alert symbol verbatim, then missing = [s for s in alert_syms if s not in prices]. The prices dict and get_quotes_batch both key on UPPER-cased symbols, and crypto detection at line 348 does s.upper() in crypto_set — but the fetched result is stored under prices[bare]=batch[pair] using the original-case bare symbol and the final comparison at line 360 uses prices.get(alert['symbol']) (original case). If an alert row's symbol is stored lower/mixed case, the uppercase batch key never matches and the alert silently never fires.
fix: Normalize once: build alert lookups on s.upper() consistently — e.g. key prices by upper, and compare cur = (prices.get(alert['symbol'].upper()) or {}).get('price'). (add_price_alert uppercases on insert today, so this is defense-in-depth against any legacy/lowercase rows.)

title: chart route: truthiness check on chart payload may skip indicators for valid-but-empty containers
description: indicators = fetcher.compute_indicators(data) if data else {}. If get_chart_data returns an empty-but-valid structure (e.g. {} with metadata, or a DataFrame/Series — which raises 'truth value is ambiguous' under bool()), the 'if data' test is either falsely False (skips indicators) or raises. For list/dict payloads it's only mildly wrong (empty data still computes nothing), but a Series/DataFrame return type would 500.
fix: Use an explicit emptiness/type check: indicators = fetcher.compute_indicators(data) if (data is not None and len(data)) else {} — or guard against ambiguous-truth types based on the documented return type of get_chart_data.

title: alt_social_pulse treats a None HN/Wiki response as 'live'
description: In the Hacker News block, hn = hn_sentiment.fetch_mentions(...) then hn.get('error') / hn.get('mention_count') are called with no None-guard; same for w = wiki_attention.fetch_pageviews(...). If either module returns None (a plausible failure/short-circuit return), hn.get(...) raises AttributeError, which is caught and reported as status 'error' — but more subtly, a returned dict with NO 'error' key but empty/None stats is marked status:'live' and then feeds _social_composite, inflating sources_live and the buzz/sentiment composite with non-data. The 'live' contract should require positive evidence, not merely 'no error key'.
fix: Guard the responses: hn = hn_sentiment.fetch_mentions(...) or {}; mark live only when it actually carries data (e.g. status 'live' iff not hn.get('error') and hn.get('mention_count')); same pattern for wikipedia (require non-empty stats/points).

title: stats() reads _mem tuple t[1] as expiry but legacy 2-tuples store (value, expiry) — fine — yet fresh count can index a concurrently-shrinking value
description: In stats(), `fresh = sum(1 for t in _mem.values() if t[1] > now)` runs under _mem_lock so iteration is safe. The subtler issue is in cache_set's LRU eviction _lru_key at line 628-630: it sorts ALL of _mem then evicts, but the sort key calls len(t) on each value tuple every comparison; if a legacy 2-tuple and 3-tuple coexist the ordering mixes last_access (3-tuple t[2]) against expiry (2-tuple t[1]) — two different clocks — so eviction can drop a recently-accessed 3-tuple entry before a stale 2-tuple one. Low impact (legacy 2-tuples are rare post-migration) but it can evict hot keys under memory pressure, causing refetch churn.
fix: Normalize legacy tuples to 3-tuples on read (cache_get already rewrites them) and, in _lru_key, anchor 2-tuples to a value that sorts them as oldest (e.g. return t[2] if len(t) >= 3 else 0.0) so a 2-tuple is always evicted before any 3-tuple with a real last_access.

title: defillama_tvl_summary sums chain TVL including negative/duplicate aggregate rows, can overstate total
description: `total = sum(float(c['tvl']) for c in all_chains_with_tvl)` sums the TVL of every chain row returned by /v2/chains. DefiLlama's chains endpoint can include aggregate or bridged-double-counted entries; more concretely it has historically returned chains with negative or null-coerced tvl that pass the isinstance(...,(int,float)) check (e.g. a transient negative). Summing those without a floor produces a 'total_tvl' that can be wrong (negative chains subtract, double-counted bridges inflate). The previous bug (summing only top-15) was fixed, but the unbounded sum has no sanity guard.
fix: Filter to positive TVL before summing: `total = sum(float(c['tvl']) for c in all_chains_with_tvl if float(c['tvl']) > 0)`, which excludes transient negatives without affecting legitimate chains.

title: get_quote reports three_month_average_volume as the 'volume' field — not current/day volume
description: The single-quote path sets `"volume": _safe(getattr(info, "three_month_average_volume", None))`, i.e. the 3-month average daily volume, but labels it 'volume' (the same key the batch path fills from a live figure and the Yahoo-direct path fills with regularMarketVolume). Consumers treating 'volume' as today's traded volume (movers, UI) get an average instead, inconsistent with every other quote source in this file. This is a real data-correctness mismatch, not just cosmetic.
fix: Use the current-volume attribute for consistency: `_safe(getattr(info, "last_volume", None)) or _safe(getattr(info, "regular_market_volume", None))`, falling back to three_month_average_volume only if those are None; or rename the field. Match the batch/Yahoo-direct semantics.

title: _finviz_quote_fallback 52W High/Low parse uses split()[0] guard that can pass an empty-then-index pattern incorrectly
description: `_num(((fund.get('52W High') or '').split() or [None])[0])`. If fund.get('52W High') is a non-empty string of only whitespace, `''.split()` returns [] -> `[] or [None]` -> [None] -> [0]=None -> _num(None)=None. Fine. But if the value is something like '12.34 - 56.78' (a range), split() yields ['12.34','-','56.78'] and [0]='12.34' — this takes the LOW end label as the high, mislabeling 52w_high/52w_low when Finviz formats the field as a range rather than a single number. The dedicated _first_num helper used in the fundamentals fallback handles this better; the quote fallback's inline parse does not.
fix: Reuse the same first-token numeric parse but validate it's the intended bound, or parse explicitly: for a 'lo - hi' range take the last token for 52W High and first for 52W Low. At minimum, share _first_num logic so range-formatted Finviz fields aren't silently mis-mapped.

title: Renormalization divides by a total that can include keys absent from raw_signals, understating applied weights
description: total_w = sum(weights.get(k, base.get(k,0.1)) for k in raw_signals) correctly sums only over available signals. But adaptive_weights returns weights renormalized to sum to total_base over ALL six components; when only a subset is available, dividing each available weight by total_w (the subset sum) is correct. The subtle bug: the per-signal `w = weights.get(key, base.get(key,0.1)) / total_w` falls back to base 0.1 for a missing key, yet total_w used the SAME fallback — so it's self-consistent. However if adaptive_weights drops a key entirely (returns dict without it), the fallback 0.1 is used in the numerator while total_w also added 0.1, so the renormalized weights still sum to 1 — OK. The real issue is only the labeling note covered separately; this entry is the lower-severity reminder that the 0.1 magic fallback differs from a component's true base weight and can skew the fusion if adaptive ever omits a present signal.
fix: Use base_weights as the single source for any missing key in BOTH the numerator and total_w (already done via _BASE_WEIGHTS.get(k, 0.1)); replace the literal 0.1 default with 0.0 or assert the key exists, since every raw_signals key is guaranteed to be in _BASE_WEIGHTS — eliminating the possibility of a phantom 0.1 weight.

category: edge case / divide by zero via sign
title: snapshot delta_pct can be computed against a previous value of opposite sign or tiny magnitude producing misleading percentages
description: In snapshot(), `delta_pct = (delta / prev['value'] * 100)` is guarded only by `prev['value']` truthiness. For series that legitimately cross zero or sit near zero (e.g. T10Y2Y 10Y-2Y spread, which is frequently between -1.0 and +1.0 and crosses 0), dividing the delta by a small or sign-flipped prev value yields wildly large or sign-inverted delta_pct (e.g. prev=-0.02, delta=0.03 → delta_pct = -150%). The macro dashboard then shows a nonsensical percentage move for spread/real-yield series. This is a real correctness issue for exactly the recession-indicator series the module highlights.
fix: Suppress or special-case delta_pct for series that can be near/cross zero (spreads, real yields): only emit delta_pct when abs(prev['value']) is above a small floor, otherwise set delta_pct to None and rely on the absolute delta. E.g. `delta_pct = (delta/prev['value']*100) if (delta is not None and prev and abs(prev['value']) > 0.5) else None`.

title: top_half_pct referenced at line 1120 may be unbound when ranks is empty
description: In _compute_peers, `top_half_pct` is only assigned inside `if ranks:` (line 1101). The else branch sets `verdict = "INSUFFICIENT DATA"` but never defines top_half_pct. The return dict at line 1120 reads `round(top_half_pct, 1) if ranks else None` — the guard `if ranks` prevents the unbound read here, so it works today, but it relies entirely on `ranks` being falsy in lockstep. This is fragile: any future code path that returns/branches differently or reads top_half_pct without the `if ranks` guard hits UnboundLocalError. The two facts (ranks empty, top_half_pct unbound) are coupled implicitly.
fix: Initialize `top_half_pct = None` before the `if ranks:` block so the name is always bound regardless of branch, and simplify line 1120 to `round(top_half_pct, 1) if top_half_pct is not None else None`.

title: _dynamic_crypto_id_map mutated without a lock from concurrent scans
description: get_full_crypto_universe runs under _full_crypto_lock, but _filtered_universe (line 261) writes `_dynamic_crypto_id_map[sym] = entry["id"]` with no lock, and _resolve_crypto_id reads it lock-free during the parallel dossier fan-out (safe_executor threads). Two idea generations in 'full' discovery mode running concurrently (or a generation racing a warmer pass) mutate this module-global dict from multiple threads. CPython's GIL makes single-item dict assignment atomic enough to avoid corruption, but there is no happens-before guarantee, so a worker can call _resolve_crypto_id for a symbol whose id another thread is mid-populating and get None, silently dropping the quote for that coin.
fix: Populate _dynamic_crypto_id_map inside the same _full_crypto_lock that guards the fetch (do the assignment in get_full_crypto_universe when building entries), or guard the read/write with a dedicated lock. At minimum, populate the map fully before fanning out the per-symbol workers.

title: warm_pool counts skip-fresh no-op passes as 0 warmed but reports errors=0 misleadingly; targets fully-skipped pass returns empty outcomes
description: When every target is filtered out by the skip-fresh logic (lines 465-470), `targets` becomes empty, parallel_map returns an empty list, and the loop at 491-495 records warmed=0, errors=0. That's correct, but warmer_status surfaces last_run_count=0 with no indication the pass was a deliberate no-op vs a total failure — the UI widget can't distinguish 'nothing to do' from 'everything failed'. More concretely: because failed targets are never persisted (per the design comment) they are never in `fresh`, so a symbol that fails every pass is retried forever and always counts toward `errors`, making last_run_errors monotonically reflect permanently-broken symbols rather than transient issues — there's no surfacing of which symbols are chronically failing.
fix: Distinguish no-op from failure in the status: when len(targets)==0 after skip-fresh, record a dedicated state (e.g. last_run_skipped == total and warmed==errors==0) and expose it. Optionally track a small set/count of chronically-failing (symbol,class,strategy) keys so last_run_errors isn't dominated by the same permanently-broken names every pass.

title: _ideas_line / _answer_ideas format NaN score with {:.0f}
description: Same root as the NaN max() issue: even setting aside max() ordering, top['composite_score'] is rendered with '{:.0f}'.format(...) and a NaN value renders literally as 'nan' in the user-facing line ('score nan'). _finite exists specifically to prevent nan/inf leaking into formatted strings (see its docstring) but is not applied on this path.
fix: After selecting top, format the score through _finite, e.g. sc = _finite(top.get('composite_score')); guard the branch on sc is not None and use sc in the format call. Combined with the filter fix this fully removes the NaN path.

title: _answer_ideas formats composite_score without finite guard
description: _answer_ideas builds 'top' via [r for r in pool if r.get('composite_score') is not None][:3] then formats each with '{:.0f}'.format(r['composite_score']). A NaN or inf score (which passes 'is not None') renders as 'nan'/'inf' in the listing, unlike the briefing's _idea_insights which uses _finite. Inconsistent guarding across the three idea-rendering sites.
fix: Filter with _finite(r.get('composite_score')) is not None and format _finite(r['composite_score']), matching _idea_insights.

title: _et_now fallback returns UTC-labeled tz-aware datetime shifted by 5h, ignoring DST and mislabeling tzinfo
description: When zoneinfo is unavailable, _et_now returns datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=5). The result still carries tzinfo=UTC but with hour/weekday values shifted as if Eastern, so any downstream .strftime('%Z') or tz-aware arithmetic treats it as UTC while the wall-clock fields are ET. It also hard-codes -5 (EST) so during DST (March-Nov) the market-phase boundaries and 'is the market open' answer are off by one hour, and near midnight .weekday() can be wrong (e.g. early UTC Monday is still Sunday ET — handled correctly only by luck of the -5 shift). This drives _market_phase and _answer_hours.
fix: Make the fallback honor DST or at least not mislabel tz: return (datetime.now(timezone.utc) - timedelta(hours=5)).replace(tzinfo=None) so it's treated as naive ET, OR compute the offset from a DST check. Minimal correctness fix: keep zoneinfo primary and, in the fallback, strip tzinfo and document it's EST-only. Given zoneinfo is in stdlib for 3.9+, consider also catching only ImportError so a transient ZoneInfo data error doesn't silently drop to the wrong-offset path.

title: Three idea-rendering paths use inconsistent NaN/None handling for composite_score
description: _idea_insights (briefing) uses _finite; _ideas_line (strip) and _answer_ideas (Q&A) use only 'is not None'. Beyond the NaN render risk already noted, this inconsistency means the same idea pool can be summarized with a different 'top' symbol depending on which surface renders it, since _finite drops inf/-inf scores that the other two keep and rank.
fix: Centralize the filter: introduce a small helper (or reuse _finite) and apply it uniformly across _idea_insights, _ideas_line, and _answer_ideas so all three agree on which scores are valid and how the top is chosen.

title: _answer_compare_quotes 'better day' winner can be reported when one change_pct is NaN
description: c1, c2 = _finite(...change_pct) guards NaN to None, and the comparison requires both not None, so NaN is handled there. However when both are None (missing change), winner stays s1 (default at line 2904) and action.symbol = s1 with no tail — acceptable. The subtler issue: when only the tail comparison is skipped, the returned action.symbol is still s1 even if s2 is the only sensible focus; minor, but the default 'winner = s1' is asserted as the navigation target regardless of data. Low impact.
fix: Default winner to None and only set action.symbol when a real winner was determined; otherwise omit symbol from the action so the UI doesn't deep-link to an arbitrarily-chosen first ticker.

title: _track_record_line hit-rate normalization misclassifies legitimate low integer percentages
description: hr_pct = hr * 100 if hr <= 1 else hr assumes any value <=1 is a fraction. A genuinely poor but already-percentage hit rate stored as e.g. 1 (1%) would be treated as the fraction 1.0 -> 100%. More plausibly, a hit rate stored as 0.0 (0% directional) hits hr <= 1 -> 0.0 (fine), but a value like 1 meaning 1% becomes 100%. The same pattern recurs in _forecast_line (line 1754). Ambiguous-units normalization is fragile when both fraction and percent representations are possible.
fix: Disambiguate on the upstream contract rather than magnitude: if forecast_accountability returns hit_rate as a fraction always, drop the conditional and use hr*100 unconditionally; if it can be either, key off a units field. At minimum gate on hr < 1 (strict) is no safer — prefer fixing the producer to emit one consistent unit.

title: _debate_ask 52-week range uses raw hi/lo without lower-bound clamp, can print negative/over-100%
description: In _debate_ask, the 52-week-range line computes (qd['price'] - lo) / (hi - lo) * 100 guarded only by 'if hi and lo and hi > lo'. Unlike _symbol_line (line 1774) which clamps with max(0, min(100, ...)), this path does not clamp, so a price below the recorded 52-week low (stale low) or above the high prints a negative or >100% range position into the LLM evidence pack and the debate prompt.
fix: Clamp consistently: line = ...; pct = max(0.0, min(100.0, (qd['price'] - lo) / (hi - lo) * 100)); use pct. Mirror the clamp already present in _symbol_line.

title: _answer_trading_agent activity coerces qty via float() without guarding non-numeric
description: In the activity branch, recent = '...'.format(..., float(o.get('qty') or 0), ...) for each order. If a tool returns qty as a non-numeric string (e.g. 'N/A') or a dict, float() raises and is caught by the broad outer except at 3932, collapsing the entire trading-agent answer into the generic 'Couldn't read the trading agent' error — losing the status/positions/performance fallbacks that would otherwise still render. One malformed order row poisons the whole response.
fix: Coerce defensively per field: wrap float(o.get('qty')) in a local helper returning 0.0 on failure (or use _finite(o.get('qty')) or 0.0), so a single bad order degrades that one entry rather than failing the whole branch.

title: available() probe cache is a non-atomic read-modify-write on module globals from concurrent request threads
description: available() reads and writes module globals _probe_at/_probe_ok without any lock. ask_stream runs in worker threads, and Flask serves requests concurrently, so two threads can interleave the 'now - _probe_at < _PROBE_TTL' check and the subsequent assignment. The effect is benign (a redundant which/ setting probe, or briefly stale True/False), but it is a genuine unsynchronized shared-state race in a web-reachable path; under load the cached value can flap.
fix: Guard the probe with a small threading.Lock (or accept staleness explicitly). Minimal fix: wrap the read-and-refresh in a module-level lock so the TTL check and the global assignment are atomic.

title: analyze limit guard 'if limit and limit > 0' silently ignores limit=0
description: if limit and limit > 0: lots = lots[:limit]. A caller passing limit=0 (meaning 'none') is treated as 'no limit' and ALL grouped sells are replayed, the opposite of the likely intent. _t_counterfactual_review never passes 0 today (it defaults to 10), but analyze is a public entry point and 0 is a plausible argument; the guard conflates 0 with unset.
fix: Decide the intended semantics and make them explicit: either 'if limit is not None and limit > 0' (treat 0/negative as unbounded, documented) or clamp limit<=0 to a sensible default; ensure the docstring matches whichever is chosen.

title: SMTP send proceeds without verifying STARTTLS succeeded when no creds, but also does not enforce TLS for the message body even when host implies TLS
description: When will_authenticate is False and starttls() raises, the code swallows the exception and continues to sendmail over a plaintext connection. The digest text/HTML (portfolio holdings, P&L, insights) is then transmitted in cleartext to the relay. The comment frames this as acceptable because there are 'no creds to leak', but the message content itself (financial positions) is sensitive and is sent unencrypted. This is a deliberate trade-off but is a real confidentiality exposure for the digest payload, not just credentials.
fix: If unencrypted transport is genuinely required for credential-less relays, gate it behind an explicit opt-in setting (e.g. smtp_allow_plaintext) and otherwise abort the send when starttls fails, so portfolio data is never silently emailed in cleartext.

title: parallel_map result is unpacked into two names without length/None validation
description: f_res, q_res = safe_executor.parallel_map(...) assumes parallel_map always returns exactly two elements. If safe_executor.parallel_map ever returns None, an empty list, or a single-element list on a degenerate internal failure, this unpack raises ValueError/TypeError, which would not be caught here (the surrounding code only guards individual fetcher calls in the non-parallel branch). The contract is documented but unenforced at this call site.
fix: Defensively coerce: results = safe_executor.parallel_map(...) or [None, None]; then f = (results[0] if len(results) > 0 else None) or {}; q = (results[1] if len(results) > 1 else None) or {}. Falls back to the empty-dict behavior the serial path already provides.

title: web_research checks the AI cap before the call but records the call only on success, under-counting failed/charged web searches
description: _web_research_uncached checks _cap_exceeded() up front, then only calls _record_ai_call() after a successful response (line 78). The OpenAI Responses web_search call is billed even when post-processing yields no usable text or when an exception is raised after the API returned. jarvis_semmem.embed deliberately records the call BEFORE validating the response shape for exactly this reason (see its comment at lines 117-120). web_research uses the opposite, looser ordering, so partially-failed or empty web searches escape the daily cap accounting and the budget can be overspent.
fix: Mirror jarvis_semmem.embed: call ai_summarizer._record_ai_call() immediately after governed_call returns (before extracting output_text / handling empties), so any billed request counts against the cap regardless of downstream parsing outcome.

title: counterfactual_review limit of 0 silently becomes 10
description: limit = int(max(1, min(n, 10))) if n else 10. _num_arg("0") returns 0.0, which is falsy, so an explicit limit=0 falls through to the default 10 rather than being treated as an (admittedly degenerate) zero or clamped to 1. Same pattern in _t_forecast/_t_price_history uses 'if n is not None' which is correct; here 'if n' is the inconsistent variant and mis-handles 0.
fix: Change the guard to 'if n is not None' and clamp: limit = int(max(1, min(n, 10))) if n is not None else 10, matching the is-not-None convention used by the other numeric tools.

title: recent_transactions flags limit_capped for 25.x even though it returns the requested ~25
description: n = int(max(1, min(requested, 25))); then 'if requested is not None and requested > 25: out["limit_capped"]=True'. A model sending 25.9 yields n=25 (effectively the full request) yet sets limit_capped/'capped at 25 (more exist)', telling the user data was withheld when it was not. Minor UX/correctness wart on the cap-surfacing logic.
fix: Compare the integer cap, not the raw float: set limit_capped only when int(requested) > 25 (or when min(requested,25) actually clamped a value the user could perceive), e.g. 'if requested is not None and requested >= 26'.

title: -USD fallback retried for any equity missing change_pct can overwrite a valid equity quote with an unrelated coin
description: _fetch_quotes retries a bare ticker as SYM-USD whenever EITHER price OR change_pct is missing/garbled (bad_chg = change_pct not a real number). Many legitimate equity quotes lack change_pct (thinly traded names, certain feeds) yet have a valid price. For such a name the code issues a SYM-USD retry; if that coin symbol resolves with price>0 it overwrites out[user_sym] with the crypto quote (line 325-326), so a price/change_pct watch on a real equity could then evaluate against an unrelated crypto instrument. The guard only checks qp>0 on the retry, not that the retried instrument is actually the same asset.
fix: Only retry -USD when the bare price itself is bad (bad_price), or when the symbol is plausibly a coin; do not trigger the overwrite solely on a missing change_pct for a name that already returned a valid positive price. Alternatively, on the change_pct-only-missing case, fill just the missing change_pct from the -USD quote rather than replacing the whole quote dict.

title: EXHAUSTION volume comparison normalizes 14d count by /2 but compares against a 7d window that overlaps the 14d window
description: _detect_phase computes `normalized_14d = cnt_14 / 2.0` and flags EXHAUSTION when `cnt_7 < normalized_14d`. But cnt_14 is the count of articles in the last 14 days, which INCLUDES the last 7 days (cnt_7). So cnt_14 = cnt_7 + cnt_8_to_14. normalized_14d = (cnt_7 + older)/2. The condition cnt_7 < (cnt_7+older)/2 simplifies to cnt_7 < older, i.e. it fires whenever the prior 7-day half had more articles than the recent 7-day half — which is the intended 'declining volume' semantics, so it's actually correct, BUT it mislabels in the boundary case where windows are built with `>= cutoff` (inclusive) so an article exactly at the 7d boundary is double counted in both windows, slightly biasing toward EXHAUSTION. Low impact.
fix: Compute the prior-week count explicitly as cnt_14 - cnt_7 and compare cnt_7 < (cnt_14 - cnt_7) so the 'declining volume' test is exact and not dependent on the /2 approximation or boundary inclusivity.

title: abnormal_return_curve: nanmean over rows that are all-NaN within the masked subset emits RuntimeWarning / NaNs
description: bench_mask keeps rows where ANY value is finite, but a kept benchmark curve can still have NaNs at some offsets (partial windows are filled with np.full(..., nan) only when entirely missing, yet _event_window_curve returns full curves or None — so this is mostly fine). However sym_arr[bench_mask] is averaged with np.nanmean over the bench-matched subset; if that subset is empty along a column (all-NaN at some offset) np.nanmean raises 'Mean of empty slice' RuntimeWarnings and yields NaN there. Not a crash but pollutes logs and produces NaN abnormal points the UI must special-case.
fix: Wrap the two nanmean calls in `with np.errstate(invalid='ignore'), warnings.catch_warnings(): warnings.simplefilter('ignore', RuntimeWarning)`, consistent with how the OLS path in research_factors silences benign numpy warnings.

title: Hypothesis due date uses naive calendar offset but horizon close lookup may read a stale prior close indefinitely on weekends/holidays
description: due = created + timedelta(days=horizon) is calendar-based by design (documented). But score_hypothesis then calls research_tracker._close_price_on_or_before(symbol, due). If `due` lands on a weekend/holiday the close-on-or-before returns the prior trading day's close — fine — but the scorer marks the hypothesis CONFIRMED/REJECTED permanently using that earlier close, even though `due` is only hours past `now`. Because resolution is permanent (status set to non-OPEN), a hypothesis whose true horizon end is a Monday gets locked to the preceding Friday close, systematically truncating multi-day-weekend horizons by up to 3 days with no re-check.
fix: When the only available close is strictly before `due` by more than ~1 trading day (i.e. the due-date bar isn't in yet), return OPEN/'still settling' instead of resolving, so the next scorer run picks up the actual due-date close once it exists — mirroring the 'no current price' OPEN path already present at line 651.

title: prob_of_target implied_return_pct uses unrounded initial_nav guard but can divide by a tiny residual
description: implied_return_pct = ((target_nav/initial_nav)-1)*100 guarded by `if initial_nav`. initial_nav comes from sim.get('initial_nav',0.0) which is the rounded surviving_mv. A surviving_mv of e.g. 0.004 rounds to 0.0 → guarded (None). But a surviving portfolio of $0.01 passes the truthiness guard and yields an absurd implied_return_pct (target/0.01). More importantly, when holdings were partially dropped, initial_nav is surviving_mv (< full portfolio), so implied_return_pct is computed against the reduced base while target_nav is the user's full-portfolio dollar target — silently overstating the implied return.
fix: Guard with a magnitude floor (`if initial_nav and abs(initial_nav) > 1e-6`) and, when dropped_symbols is non-empty, either compute implied_return_pct against the original full initial_nav or annotate that the figure is relative to the surviving NAV only.

title: _build_note 'premium cheap/expensive' verdict can read backwards vs edge_score for tiny implied moves
description: _build_note guards `implied <= 0.01` but for small-but-positive implied (e.g. 0.05%) it computes `ratio = historical/implied`, which can be huge, producing 'historical N% larger than implied — premium cheap' with N in the thousands. Meanwhile _edge_score clamps to ±3 with denom `max(abs(implied),1.0)`, so for the same event edge_score is near 0 (because the 1.0 floor dominates) while the note screams 'premium cheap'. The two fields then tell contradictory stories for low-implied events.
fix: Use the same denominator floor in the note as in _edge_score: gate the ratio verdict on `implied >= 1.0` (or compute the verdict from the already-clamped edge_score) so the note and edge_score agree for tiny implied moves rather than the note exploding while edge_score stays muted.

title: Non-numeric narrative velocity can raise in comparison
description: _component_narrative does `velocity = result.get("velocity_score") or 0` then `fired = (...) or velocity >= 40` (and `<= -40`). The `or 0` only guards None/0/empty; if narrative_engine ever returns a non-numeric truthy velocity_score (e.g. a label string), `velocity >= 40` raises TypeError. It's caught by the component wrapper so it degrades to fired=False, but it silently disables a real signal. Other modules (_safe_float) coerce velocity defensively; this one does not.
fix: Coerce defensively: replace `velocity = result.get("velocity_score") or 0` with a float coercion, e.g. `try: velocity = float(result.get("velocity_score") or 0) except (TypeError, ValueError): velocity = 0.0`.

title: Tanh squash factor differs from documented contract (2.0 vs 1.6)
description: The module docstring and the inline comment at 648-650 specify the final transform `50 + 50*tanh(weighted_avg*2)` (and claim |avg|=0.5 -> ~83), but the code uses `score = 50.0 + 50.0 * _tanh(avg * 1.6)`. With 1.6, |avg|=0.5 lands at ~73, not 83, and the published API contract is wrong. Either the factor or the docstring is incorrect — they disagree, so the scoring scale a consumer expects is wrong.
fix: Reconcile the two: if 1.6 is the intended calibration, update the docstring (lines 21-23) and the 648-650 comment to say `tanh(avg*1.6)` and the correct anchor (~73). If 2.0 was intended, change line 651 to `_tanh(avg * 2.0)`. Pick one and make code and docs match.

title: _dynamic_weight dereferences track-record result outside its try block
description: The try/except at 194-198 wraps only the `get_track_record` call; the subsequent `n = int(rec.get("n_directional") or 0)` (line 199) and `hit = rec.get("hit_rate")` run outside it. research_tracker.get_track_record always returns a dict today (so no crash now), but if any future/alternate tracker implementation or a monkeypatch returns None, `rec.get` raises AttributeError that escapes _dynamic_weight and aborts the whole _compute (the per-contributor try at 605-609 only wraps fn(symbol), not _dynamic_weight at 622). The defensive intent of the surrounding code is undermined by the narrow try scope.
fix: Either extend the try to cover the dereference, or guard explicitly: after the try, add `if not isinstance(rec, dict): return static_w, None, 0` before reading n_directional/hit_rate.

title: Insider 60-day window mixes local-time naive datetime with UTC epoch cutoff
description: _insider_form4_net_60d builds `cutoff_ts = time.time() - 60*86400` (UTC epoch seconds) but compares against `dt_obj.timestamp()` where dt_obj came from `datetime.strptime(...,'%Y-%m-%d')` — a NAIVE datetime that `.timestamp()` interprets in the host's LOCAL timezone. On any non-UTC host the 60-day boundary drifts by the UTC offset (hours), so a filing right at the edge is mis-included/excluded. The sibling modules (synth_cluster, opportunity_scanner) deliberately anchor these windows to ET/naive consistently; this one is inconsistent.
fix: Compare dates in the same naive frame instead of via .timestamp(): `cutoff_dt = datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(days=60)` and `if dt_obj < cutoff_dt: continue`. (Drop cutoff_ts and the .timestamp() call.)

title: Base-rate hit_rate ignores cosine-distance weighting and treats opposite-direction analogs equally
description: _base_rate computes `hit_rate = sum(hits)/len(hits)` over the k nearest analogs, but a tracker 'hit' is recorded relative to that analog's OWN predicted_direction (stored per row). The current pattern is matched by cosine similarity, which is high for both same-direction AND exactly-opposite-direction vectors only when shared dims align in sign — but cosine distance up to 2 means some retained analogs are anti-correlated with the current pattern. Averaging their raw hit flags (which describe whether THAT past call worked, not whether it aligns with the current bullish/bearish tilt) yields a base rate that doesn't actually describe 'what happens to patterns like mine'. An anti-correlated analog that 'hit' (its bearish call worked) inflates a bullish-pattern base rate.
fix: Either restrict analogs to those whose pattern_distance is below a similarity floor (e.g. distance < 1.0, i.e. positive cosine sim) before computing the base rate, or re-orient each analog's outcome by the sign of its similarity to the current pattern (flip realized_return/hit for anti-correlated analogs) so the base-rate summary reflects same-direction analogs.

title: Portfolio expected_5d uses all factors but IQR/best/worst band only scales SPY by market beta
description: _portfolio_projection computes `expected_5d_pct = Σ beta_f * avg_factor_return_5d[f]` across ALL factors (Mkt-RF, SMB, HML, RMW, CMA, Mom), but the surrounding band (`iqr_5d`, `best_case`, `worst_case`) is derived purely from the SPY 5-day distribution scaled by the single market beta. For a portfolio with large non-market factor tilts, the point estimate can fall outside its own [worst_case, best_case] band, which is internally contradictory and will render as a nonsensical cone in the UI.
fix: Make the band consistent with the point estimate: either compute expected_5d from the market-beta-scaled SPY mean as well (so it lies within the SPY-derived band), or widen the band to reflect the full multi-factor projection (e.g. scale the SPY IQR by total absolute factor contribution rather than only mkt_beta). At minimum clamp the reported expected_5d into [worst_case, best_case] when both are present.

title: Narrative phase falls back to topic bucket that the composite's BULL/BEAR test can never match
description: _narrative_panel sets `phase = n.get("narrative_phase") or n.get("dominant_narrative")`. dominant_narrative is a topic bucket (GROWTH, REGULATORY, SCANDAL, ...), not a directional label. In _composite_score the phase contribution is keyed on `"BULL" in phase` / `"BEAR" in phase` (lines 571-574). When narrative_phase is absent and the fallback dominant_narrative bucket is used, that bucket string will essentially never contain 'BULL'/'BEAR', so the fallback silently contributes nothing — and worse, a clearly bearish bucket like SCANDAL/REGULATORY is treated as neutral. The sibling modules (synth_cluster, synth_divmap) explicitly map buckets to direction; sectorflow does not for this fallback.
fix: When falling back to dominant_narrative, translate the bucket to a direction the composite can read (mirror synth_divmap's _NARRATIVE_BULL/_NARRATIVE_BEAR sets), or have _composite_score map known bullish/bearish buckets in addition to the BULL/BEAR substring test, so the fallback phase actually feeds the score.
